entities.name: PurQ
observations: The 221-residue query sequence is an exact sequence match to reviewed Deinococcus radiodurans phosphoribosylformylglycinamidine synthase subunit PurQ, with 100% identity and full coverage.
PurQ is a type-I glutamine amidotransferase; Pfam matches GATase_5 (PF13507) and GATase_3 (PF07685).
The conserved catalytic nucleophile is at position 87 in the exact reference annotation.
PurQ is the glutaminase component of the FGAM synthase complex and supplies ammonia generated from glutamine hydrolysis to PurL.

entities.name: PurQ glutamine hydrolysis
observations: L-glutamine + H2O → L-glutamate + NH4(+); Rhea RHEA:15889.
This is the direct glutaminase reaction performed by PurQ to generate ammonia for FGAM synthesis.

entities.name: FGAM synthesis
observations: N(2)-formyl-N(1)-(5-phospho-beta-D-ribosyl)glycinamide + L-glutamine + ATP + H2O → 2-formamido-N(1)-(5-O-phospho-beta-D-ribosyl)acetamidine + L-glutamate + ADP + phosphate + H(+); Rhea RHEA:17129.
The overall reaction is carried out by the PurL/PurQ/PurS complex; PurQ hydrolyzes glutamine, while PurL transfers the resulting ammonia to FGAR and uses ATP.

entities.name: De novo purine biosynthesis
observations: PurQ participates in the ATP-dependent FGAM synthetase step of de novo IMP biosynthesis.
